text.text: Your immigration practice in one place. Start with Notices that need action today or this week, check each Case and its response date, and chase evidence items from clients. Operational tracking only; it holds no legal advice, and the date printed on each notice controls.
Notices arrive in many forms. Log each one the same day.
Press Log notice on the case and choose the kind.
Copy the due date exactly as printed on the notice.
Enter it in two places: here and the firm calendar.
Draft the response a week ahead.
Attorney reviews at least three days before the due date.
Mark Done when the filing receipt is saved.
Book an interpreter if the client prefers another language.
Explain fees and the engagement agreement in plain language.
Create the case and attach the document checklist.
Use Add evidence item for every item the client must bring.
Set Needed by dates a week before the filing target.
Mark Verified only after a second person has checked names and dates.
Many malpractice insurers expect deadlines to be recorded in two places.
Review Notices due this week with the attorney
Compare this table with the firm calendar
Check cases without a receipt number after filing
Check approved and closed cases for follow-up work
Call or message the client in their preferred language.
Explain what the notice means in one or two sentences, and what they must do.
Note the update on the notice.
Send each active client a short status message, even when nothing has changed.
